transcript_tail.text: Running `audit-suggest.sh` against dstrader-docker, passing the latest report so Claude can spot near-misses too.
The awk substitution chokes on multi-line `-v` variables. Swapping to a Python one-liner that handles multi-line literal replacement cleanly.
`claude -p` is going to take a minute on a prompt this size — running in background, I'll come back when it returns.

Claude proposed 12 new rules, all evidence-grounded with specific file references in the rationale. Quick triage:

**Critical (3):**
- `encr-file-tracked` — catches `*.encr` ciphertext (the original incident class, current rule only covers `.pgp/.asc/.gpg`)
- `passphrase-file-tracked` — `dstrader.passphrase` and similar naming patterns
- `vnc-passwd-tracked` — VNC passwd files (trivially reversible obfuscation)

**High (8):**
- `ib-auto-login-credentials` — `actualLiveLogin=…` / `loginPasswordHash=…` keys (archetypes.md called these out; rules.yaml only had `actualLiveAccount`)
- `jdbc-url-with-credentials` — embedded `jdbc:driver://user:pass@host`
- `log4j-smtp-credentials` — `log4j2.xml` SMTP appender password (XML, not `.properties` — missed by existing rule)
- `gpg-passphrase-flag-literal` — `gpg --passphrase=<literal>` (skips `--passphrase-fd/-file/-repeat`)
- `openssl-pass-literal` — `openssl -pass pass:<literal>`
- `smtplib-login-literal` — Python `SMTP.login(user, "literal")`
- `cron-mysql-password-arg` — `mysql -p<literal>` in extensionless `cron_root` files (existing rule paths only `.sh/.yml/.yaml`)
- `shell-env-script-tracked` — committed `local.env.sh` (current rule globs `.env*`, misses `.env.sh`)

**Medium (2):**
- `gnupg-bind-mount-in-compose` — bind-mount of host `~/.gnupg`/`.ssh`/`.aws` into containers
- `non-image-in-image-dir` — generalizes `misplaced-pdf-in-images` to `.txt/.csv/.log/.doc/.docx`

Every proposal cites a specific path or evidence in the repo. The model correctly noticed gaps like `cron_root` being extensionless and `log4j2.xml` being a different XML shape than `.properties` — both genuine blindspots in my hand-written rules.

The AI rules found 4 real findings the hand-written ruleset missed — exactly what they were designed to do:

- **`.encr` ciphertext files** (3): `dstrader/prod/auto_login.properties{,.dstrader-p1,.dtogni789}.encr` — this is the original critical class from HISTORY-AUDIT.md §2 row 1. Pulled out of history during the scrub but still in HEAD because the GPG-backed auto-login uses them until the SOPS cutover (#11) lands.
- **`dstrader/dstrader.passphrase`** — the GPG passphrase file the runbook says to remove in Phase 3c.

These aren't fixable here; they're the GPG-retirement blockers already tracked by #11 in the go-public epic. The audit pipeline now correctly surfaces them. Committing the merged ruleset.

Final scan with the full ruleset finds 5 things, all expected:
- **1**: `jump_server/wake_dstrader.sh` MAC — already fixed in the bridge branch above
- **4**: GPG retirement blockers (`*.encr` × 3, `dstrader.passphrase`) — tracked by `dstrader-aws#11`, gated on SOPS cutover, will resolve in Phase 3c of the runbook

The AI step justified itself: every one of its 13 proposals was evidence-grounded and accepted on first read, and it correctly surfaced the `.encr` class which is the original critical finding the hand-written rules had a gap on.
